title: rwb-access next action: the role-catalogue operation, the authorise request and answer of a next-action read, the rwb-access login and the message for an unknown role code are not specified
source: Context pack P4 rwb-access (service row, ownership rows, slides 10 and 13); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1, T6.2 and appendix T-A.1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.3, A2.4 and A2.14; Legacy RWB-E2-035 sections 3, 10, 12 and 13
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow; section 5 Exception path X5; section 11 Data; section 12.2, 12.8 and 12.9 Contract; section 13 Solution plan; section 14 Validation and messages
description: Four values this slice needs are absent. (1) No source names an operation that answers the role name and class of a role code, although legacy section 12 calls ReferenceData.role(roleCode) for roleName and roleClass and TSD P4 T3.1 holds role_name and role_class; the ownership rows give rwb-access four operations only (GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants), and API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles declares Platform administration R, which no service identity holds in T6.1. (2) Architecture v5 names POST /authorise (cached) as the access path and the TSD appendix has no authorise entry, so the attributes a next-action request carries (case, owner, team, queue role, field IDs) and the fields the answer returns are a read, not a source value. (3) The per-service database login for rwb-access is named nowhere. (4) No message is defined for a role code with no row in force.
evidence: Context pack P4 lists the four provided operations above and no role read; TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no authorise path, and API-P4-007 is the only role read and is Platform administration R; TSD P4 T6.1 gives SY-CASEWF '-' for Platform administration; TSD P4 T3.1 defines role_name and role_class with no read operation; Legacy RWB-E2-035 section 12 names ReferenceData.role(roleCode) and section 13 names no login; FSD P4 A2.7 requires every read of a case to be logged and defines no access-entry field set for a next-action read.
area: rwb-access contract, runtime configuration and messages
proposed: Add GET /api/recovery/access/v1/role-catalogue/{roleCode} with its answer schema to the API specification and TSD P4 appendix T-A, publish it with RWB-P4-E1037-CON and stub it in that contract fake, fix the authorise request and answer schema of a next-action read in the same appendix, fix the rwb-access login in the platform DB story, and add the message for an unknown or inactive role code to the message catalogue.

title: rwb-access next action: the role class list has no customer-party value, while the legacy waiting text is produced for a customer party or a partner user
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.2 LOV-ROLE-CLASS and T3.1 role.role_class; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 field catalog of A2.3, A2.4 and A2.14; Legacy RWB-E2-035 business rule BR5 and acceptance criterion AC3
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Background, AC4, AC5 and AC6; section 8 Business rule BR4; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Legacy BR5 makes the next action a wait when the owner role is of class Customer party or Partner user and the text starts 'Waiting for {owner}:', and legacy AC3 shows it with owner role CU-BORROW and the words 'Waiting for Customer (borrower):'. The role class list in force is LOV-ROLE-CLASS with three values, BANK_USER, PARTNER_USER and NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, and the field catalog describes them as bank user, partner user and non-human actor, so the customer-party class that CU-BORROW needs has no value in the list and the class of a customer role cannot be read from a source.
evidence: TSD P4 T3.2 LOV-ROLE-CLASS reads 'BANK_USER, PARTNER_USER, NON_HUMAN_ACTOR'; TSD P4 T3.1 DF-REF-037 is role_class varchar(15) on LOV-ROLE-CLASS; FSD P4 A2.3 and A2.4 field catalogs read 'role.role_class | Bank user, partner user, non-human actor | varchar(15)'; Legacy RWB-E2-035 BR5 names Customer party and Partner user and AC3 shows 'Waiting for Customer (borrower):' with owner role CU-BORROW.
area: rwb-access role catalogue and role classes
proposed: Add CUSTOMER_PARTY to LOV-ROLE-CLASS as a fourth value in the same load that carries the roles and let the customer-party roles carry it, so the waiting class is data; confirm the value with the role catalogue owner before the policy pack of wave 2 goes in force.

title: rwb-access next action: the RBAC matrix tabulates three capability areas and gives no Case record letter, so the R rights and the scopes the next-action read needs are not tabulated
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 and T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and A2.14; Legacy RWB-E2-035 authority table, business rules BR6 and BR9 and acceptance criterion AC13
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Background; section 8 Business rules BR1 and BR6; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The next-action read is decided in the CASE_RECORD capability area, and legacy AC13 proves the refusal of a role with no Case record R. TSD P4 T6.1 tabulates Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration only, so no role has a Case record letter in a source table, and the default scope the scope rule compares is never tabulated either; the letters of RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-COMPLAIN and RW-AUDIT and the default scope of the specialist roles therefore come from the policy pack as data. Legacy BR9 also depends on the queue role of a case, which is queue.role_code and belongs to P3.
evidence: TSD P4 T6.1 headers read 'Role | Rules and parameters | Reference data | Platform administration' from RW-CASEOWN to SY-AGENT; LOV-CAPABILITY in T3.2 lists CASE_RECORD and 13 other areas; LOV-SCOPE in T3.2 lists OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL with no per-role value; Legacy RWB-E2-035 AC13 refuses RW-REFADM with MSG-P4-002 and BR9 reads queue.role_code.
proposed: Extend the T6.1 matrix with the Case record column for every role, publish the full 14-area matrix version as data through RWB-P4-AD002-APP, and fix the default scope of the specialist roles with the security administrator before PM-2026.12 goes in force.

title: rwb-access next action: a role row carries no version label of its own and the lifetime of a cached access or role answer is not specified
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (role, permission and masking_rule field sets); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 acceptance criteria of A2.4; Legacy RWB-E2-035 section 13 and business rule BR10; Decoupling pattern DP-11
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 8 and 9; section 7 AC7; section 8 Business rule BR8; section 12.3 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data and Build step 5
description: The role catalogue answer has to name the version its rows came from, because the legacy story records the version that set a value and never rewrites it (BR10) and the FSD changes a policy by loading a new version. The role table has no version column: only permission.matrix_version and masking_rule.masking_version carry a label, and the standard record columns give no valid_from on role. No source fixes the lifetime of a cached access answer either. This story therefore names the matrix version in force as the catalogue version and drops both caches on the policy event, and it fixes no lifetime.
evidence: TSD P4 T3.1 role fields are id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope and entra_group with no version; DF-REF-044 matrix_version sits on permission and DF-REF-202 masking_version on masking_rule; T3.0 standard columns are is_active, state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at and updated_by; FSD P4 AC-P4-004-01 changes a policy by loading version PM-2026.12; no parameter for a cache lifetime appears in TSD P4 or FSD P4.
proposed: State in the TSD that the role rows are versioned by the matrix version they are loaded with, or add a role_version label to the load; fix the cache lifetime as a parameter of the parameters contract (DP-06) with its value agreed at the wave 2 design review, and test the version-keyed drop rather than the clock.
